text:
Democrats on Wednesday nominated Hakeem Jeffries to serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress begins next year.
A New York congressman who has served as the Democratic minority leader since 2023, Jeffries is set to become one of Donald Trump’s most prominent opponents for the final two years of his presidency, when Democrats will control both the Senate and House of Representatives and undertake aggressive efforts to check his powers.
Jeffries was nominated despite concerns from some progressives that he represents a politically risky status quo for a party that is looking to capitalize on a surprisingly good performance in the midterms, where voters swept them back into power in both the House and Senate with significant majorities.
Jeffries is set to be formally elected speaker when the House of Representatives convenes at the beginning of next year, with Democrats controlling a majority of at least 257 seats, their largest in nearly two decades. The 56-year-old would become the first Black lawmaker to serve as House speaker, and the first Democrat since Nancy Pelosi, who is set to retire from Congress at the end of this year.
No other Democrat stood against Jeffries for the job, and his party nominated him by a recorded vote at their behind-closed-doors caucus meeting. They also selected California congressman Ted Lieu to serve as caucus chair.
In office since 2013, Jeffries was House Democratic caucus chair when Pelosi served as speaker from 2019 to 2023. He took over as leader when she stepped down after Democrats lost their House majority in 2022, but rankled progressives by refusing to endorse proposals to create a Medicare for All healthcare system, and for not taking a strong stance against aid to Israel amid accusations it carried out a genocide in Gaza. Earlier this month, Indivisible, a nationwide progressive organizing group, released a poll that found only 28% of registered voters view Jeffries favorably.
He’s recently sought to bridge those divides, and on Tuesday announced his support for lowering the age of eligibility for Medicare, and expanding its coverage to include vision and dental treatments, and to offer it to children. He’s also called for “dramatic change” in the US relationship with Israel, though in July did not vote for an amendment that would have cut military aid to the Middle Eastern ally.
In the run-up to the vote, Don Leonard, a newly elected Democrat representing an Ohio district Donald Trump won in the 2024 election, told CNN he wouldn’t vote for Jeffries unless he won commitments to end aid to Israel, and undo the supreme court’s Citizens United ruling, which allowed outside groups to spend unlimited amounts on elections.
Shortly before the vote, he confirmed to the network that because Jeffries had not met his demands, he wouldn’t vote for him.
